blocks.content: The Competition Act, 2002 marked a paradigm shift from curbing monopolies to promoting healthy market competition in India.

rows: Promoting fair competition and market freedom
Market power and abuse of dominant position
Cease-and-desist powers with limited penal action
Direct heavy monetary fines up to 10% of turnover

items: The S.V.S. Raghavan Committee (2000) laid the structural foundation for replacing the MRTP Act with the Competition Act, 2002.
CCI enforces the 'Effects Doctrine' under Section 32, giving it extra-territorial jurisdiction over acts outside India that impact domestic competition.
Dominance under MRTP was strictly asset-size based, whereas under CCI it is conduct-based (abuse of dominant position).

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The MRTP Act, 1969 focused primarily on controlling monopolies and preventing the concentration of economic power.
The Raghavan Committee (2000) recommended replacing the outdated MRTP framework with a modern competition law suited for liberalized markets.
The Competition Act, 2002 led to the creation of the Competition Commission of India (CCI), shifting regulatory focus to market conduct rather than market size.
Unlike the MRTP Commission which had limited penalty powers, CCI can levy penalties up to 10% of average turnover for anti-competitive agreements.
The MRTP Commission was formally dissolved in 2009, transferring its pending matters to the Competition Appellate Tribunal (COMPAT).
